plan: To prioritize capital preservation, we will sell all leveraged ETFs: METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, and MUU.
This eliminates high-risk exposure and aligns with the conservative mandate.
We will also trim SPY to 20% to cure the concentration mandate breach.
This strategy focuses on reducing overall portfolio risk and maintaining a cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. Expect lower volatility and reduced drawdown risk, but also limited upside potential.

plan: For a balanced approach, we will trim all leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
This reduces overall portfolio leverage and risk.
SPY will be trimmed to 20% to address the concentration mandate.
We will add NVDD at 4% as a high-quality scanner long setup to introduce targeted growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month growth with a risk-first approach. It balances growth potential with reduced leverage, aiming for moderate volatility and drawdown.

plan: For aggressive growth, we will trim SPY to 20% to cure the concentration mandate breach.
We will add NVDD at 6%, SPXS at 6%, and AAPU at 6% from the strongest scanner long setups.
This strategy leans into high-conviction setups and uses leverage for amplified returns.
Strict stops will be maintained to manage increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by leveraging high-conviction setups. Be aware of significantly higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs.

plan: To prioritize income, we will sell all leveraged ETFs: METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, and MUU.
This eliminates high-beta exposure not aligned with income generation.
SPY will be trimmed to 20% to address the concentration mandate.
We will add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced monthly distributions.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on steady distributions and capital preservation. While aiming for low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
